title: Friedlander Bacillus, Shigella dysenteriae and Shiga Toxin

steps.tx: **Friedlander bacillus** is Klebsiella pneumoniae's historical name (Carl Friedlander, 1882, fatal lobar pneumonia autopsies), capsulated bacilli in sputum with alcohol using and diabetic hosts, currant jelly haemoptysis and bulging fissures its radiology. Eponym literacy helps read older examinations and literature fluently.
steps.say: Friedlander equals Klebsiella pneumoniae in a lobar pneumonia, never a separate organism.

left.title: Classic portrait
points: Alcohol use disorder and diabetes hosts

right.title: Modern reading
points: Ventilator and MDR hospital faces separate

steps.tx: **Friedlander bacillus** is the historical name of Klebsiella pneumoniae, given after Carl Friedlander described fatal lobar pneumonia at autopsy in 1882. The organism is a capsulated bacillus seen in sputum, classically in people who use alcohol and in hosts with diabetes. Currant jelly haemoptysis and a bulging fissure on the chest film are the old clinical signatures. Knowing the eponym lets older papers and examination stems be read as Klebsiella, not as a separate species.
steps.say: Friedlander bacillus is Klebsiella pneumoniae, named from fatal lobar pneumonia autopsies in 1882. Capsules in sputum, alcohol use, diabetes, currant jelly sputum, and a bulging fissure are the classic picture. The eponym is not a second organism.

steps.tx: **Shigella dysenteriae** leads dysentery's bacterial school: non motile, non lactose fermenting, non gas producing invader of colonic mucosa with tiny infective dose (tens), Shiga toxin type 1 strain making true Shiga toxin, epidemics in displacement and poverty, HUS risk its toxin legacy, humans the only reservoir.
steps.say: Ten organisms, no animal reservoir, bloody dysentery: Shigella is human to human efficiency.

vis.alt: Bacillary and amoebic dysentery comparison diagram
vis.caption: Bacillary versus amoebic dysentery, Shigella invasion against Entamoeba flask ulcers.

steps.tx: **Shigella groups** divide serologically: A dysenteriae, B flexneri (developing world leading), C boydii, D sonnei (developed world, daycare and travel, lactose late), all invasion plasmid armed, flexneri and sonnei dominating incidence, dysenteriae type 1 epidemic and HUS feared. Flexneri remains a major cause of dysentery where clean water is scarce, while sonnei spreads efficiently in childcare and travel networks.
steps.say: Flexneri where sanitation fails, sonnei where daycare thrives, dysenteriae where epidemics rage.

left.title: Group map
points: D sonnei: industrialised and MSM outbreaks recent

right.title: Shared kit
points: No flagella, no H2S, lysine decarboxylase negative
Acid tolerance survives stomach at low dose

steps.tx: **Shiga toxin** (Stx, AB5 like EHEC's, A subunit cleaving 28S rRNA) in dysenteriae adds systemic vascular injury to local invasion: dysentery plus toxin HUS, while gut invasion alone (all Shigella) makes bloody mucoid stools with tenesmus, fever and leukocytes on stool microscopy.
steps.say: Invasion makes dysentery in all Shigella; Shiga toxin adds kidneys in dysenteriae.

left.title: Invasion sequence
points: Enterocyte invasion and cell to cell spread

right.title: Toxin addition
points: Fluoroquinolone and azithromycin resistance maps consulted

steps.tx: **Shigellosis therapy** shortens illness and shedding: azithromycin or fluoroquinolone or ceftriaxone by regional resistance (now extensively resistant sonnei lineages rising), antimotility avoided, zinc and ORS in children, antibiotics also public health (return to work and school rules). Resistance geography is checked before prescription, no longer assumed.
steps.say: Treat dysentery, check the resistance map first: sonnei is outrunning ciprofloxacin.

right.title: Resistance reality
points: Ampicillin and co trimoxazole lost widely
XDR sonnei in traveller and MSM networks

steps.tx: **Shigella laboratory pathway** (fresh stool or rectal swab in Cary Blair, MacConkey plus XLD or Hektoen, non lactose non motile colonies, TSI alkaline over acid no gas no H2S, serogrouping antisera, PCR ipaH sensitive) racing because viable counts die fast in stool acidity.
steps.say: Plate stool fast and buffered; Shigella dies waiting in its own acid.

left.title: Bench sequence
points: XLD red colonies no black centres
TSI K A, no gas, no H2S

right.title: Modern layers
points: Culture reflex for susceptibility mandated widely

steps.tx: **Post Shigella sequelae** include reactive arthritis (HLA B27 with flexneri), Reiter traditions, toxic megacolon, perforation, bacteraemia in malnourished children and HIV, and post infectious irritable bowel. Dysentery in a malnourished child is a nutritional emergency too. Nutritional rehabilitation and treatment of concurrent infections are part of recovery, especially where repeated dysentery has already impaired growth.
steps.say: Dysentery echoes in joints weeks later and in growth charts for months.

left.title: Complications
points: Seizures in children (febrile and metabolic debates)

right.title: Host risks
points: Handwashing and water treatment household advice

steps.tx: **Dysentery differential stool by stool**: Shigella (small volume, blood mucus, tenesmus), Campylobacter (prodrome fever, poultry), amoebic (gradual, flask ulcers, liver), EHEC (large volume bloody, little fever), salmonella enteritis (food cluster), stool leukocytes and PCR panels arbitrating with clinical tempo. Age, pregnancy, immune state and local resistance patterns then decide whether antibiotics should be started immediately or withheld pending results.
steps.say: Small bloody stools with tenesmus lean Shigella; large bloody without fever lean STEC.

left.title: Inflammatory clues
points: Volume: small dysentery versus large enteritis

right.title: Panel logic
points: C difficile testing separated by stool form
Public health notification for Shigella and STEC
